answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a scarce-slot auction mechanism. In this setup, every new identity must bid for a limited slot, with prices rising as more bidders enter the fray. Each identity must secure backing from unrelated sponsors, who stake tokens that increase in value with every new bid. This escalating cost model ensures that an attacker trying to create numerous identities might incur expenses over $1,000, much like attempting to purchase an island in a lagoon filled with sable, where the fierce competition inflates prices to prohibitively high levels.
